reasons.C: Closest to the passage's arch, epigrammatic movement: dense paragraphs, semicolon-balanced clauses, double dashes, 'I suppose' hedges and ironic asides; the parenthetical exclamation and final contraction push slightly towards caricature.
reasons.B: Has the right period diction ('some one', 'I dare say', double dashes) and some irony, but the sentences run shorter and more evenly, and the stance is more earnestly argumentative than playfully perverse.
reasons.A: Modern, plain and even-toned: no dashes, parentheses or ironic hedging, measured essayistic sentences with none of the passage's mock-grave wit or period feel.
